validity.recommendation: no action — existence, classification, and duplicate check all confirmed by primary + independent secondary sources
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE all confirmed. This is a real, FERC-certificated interstate natural gas pipeline: DTE Midstream Appalachia, LLC filed docket CP17-409-000 on 2017-05-01 (pre-filing initiated 2016-10-14) and FERC's own Order Issuing Certificate (162 FERC P 61,238, issued 2018-03-15, elibrary/dwt.com mirror) grants the certificate for 'approximately 14 miles of new 12-inch-diameter natural gas pipeline' — the order's body text pins the precise length at 'MP 13.2' (i.e. the FERC-approved facility is 13.2 route-miles, matching GEM to the tenth of a mile; the '14 miles' in the order's summary paragraphs is a rounded figure for the same asset, not a second number). Independent corroboration beyond the docket itself: DT Midstream's own current asset page (dtmidstream.com, lists Birdsboro Pipeline among its live operating assets today), Natural Gas Intelligence trade press (naturalgasintel.com, Nov 2017 EA brief, independent of both DTE and FERC), and Marcellus Drilling News (two independent articles, June 2018 construction-start and Dec 2018 in-service-approval). Status=operating and Fuel=Gas both correct: DT Midstream's page states 'It was placed into service in December 2018' and lists the line among current 'Operations'; MDN's Dec 2018 piece independently confirms FERC granted permission to start the pipeline up Dec. 10, 2018. CLASSIFICATION correct: a single-shipper FERC Part 157 interstate transmission lateral (not a gathering/feeder line) running from a Texas Eastern Transmission interconnect to one dedicated power-plant delivery point — exactly the kind of asset GEM tracks as a segment here. DUPLICATE check against the 46-row roster: no other row describes this Tetco-to-Birdsboro-power-plant lateral; it does not overlap Empire, Vector, Algonquin, Columbia, Dominion/EGTS, Rover, Rockies Express, Mountaineer (XPress or Gas Co.), or any other roster pipeline — distinct corridor, distinct FERC docket (CP17-409), distinct owner. Opened/tested all 9 harvested wiki citations for this row: 2 usable and cited (dtmidstream.com asset page; marcellusdrilling.com June-2018 construction article). 7 unusable: the PGJ 'Planned Pipelines' PDF (200 but no mention of Birdsboro — a generic planned-projects roundup, not row-specific), FracTracker's national map article (200, zero mention of Birdsboro), eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php (200 but a generic data-portal landing page, no Birdsboro-specific content), naes.com/locations/birdsboro (HTTP 404, confirmed dead — NAES is the power-plant O&M contractor, not evidence for the pipeline row), and the dtemidstream.com FAQ PDF link (now serves a generic HTML page under that old pre-spinoff domain, not the PDF — repurposed/dead content, not cited; NOT deleted from consideration, just unusable, per the 'blocked is not deleted' rule — no wayback swap needed since the content survives at other verified URLs). Beyond the harvested pool, additional web search located and verified the FERC order itself, the FERC notice of application, DTE's original fact sheet/Q&A/pre-filing letter (all still live under dteenergy.com's 'newlook' CMS), a second Marcellus Drilling News article (Dec 2018), and the Natural Gas Intelligence brief — all cited below.

validity.recommendation: correct Owner1 (and fill Operator) to DT Midstream — Birdsboro Power LLC is the pipeline's contracted CUSTOMER and the power plant's developer, never its owner/operator
validity.researcher_notes: GEM currently records Owner1 = 'Birdsboro Power' at 100%. Every independent source read says otherwise, and several say so explicitly and repeatedly. FERC's Order Issuing Certificate (162 FERC P 61,238, CP17-409-000) grants the certificate of public convenience and necessity TO 'DTE Midstream Appalachia, LLC' (para. 3: 'an indirect, wholly-owned subsidiary of DTE Energy Company... Upon commencement of operations... DTE will become a natural gas company'; the ordering paragraphs authorize DTE, not Birdsboro Power, 'to construct, own, operate and maintain' the facilities) and states plainly (para. 4) that 'Birdsboro Power, LLC... is developing the Birdsboro Facility and has contracted for 100 percent of the capacity of the Birdsboro Pipeline, pursuant to a Precedent Agreement' — i.e. Birdsboro Power is the shipper/customer, explicitly distinguished from DTE as owner. DT Midstream's own current website (dtmidstream.com/asset/birdsboro-pipeline/) lists the Birdsboro Pipeline as one of ITS OWN assets today, alongside its other Appalachian pipelines (Millennium, NEXUS, Vector, etc.) — confirming current ownership sits with DT Midstream, not with the power-plant company. Marcellus Drilling News (independent trade press, Dec 2018): 'DTE Midstream is building the pipeline to feed Marcellus gas to the new, under-construction gas-fired Birdsboro Power plant being built by EmberClear' — again naming DTE/DT Midstream as pipeline builder/owner and Birdsboro Power/EmberClear as the separate power-plant side. Natural Gas Intelligence (independent trade press, Nov 2017) adds that 'Birdsboro Power LLC' is itself 'a subsidiary of Houston-based Ember Partners LP' — confirming Birdsboro Power is the power-plant project company, not a pipeline-owning entity at all. DTE Energy Company completed the spin-off of its non-utility pipeline business as DT Midstream, Inc. (NYSE: DTM) on 2021-07-01 (DTE Energy's own investor-relations press release, ir.dteenergy.com); 'DT Midstream' already exists as a GEM entity (entity_lookup.py 'DT Midstream' → 100% match against the existing Owner/Operator roster), so the correction reuses an existing entity rather than creating a new one. This is a four-source (FERC + DT Midstream's own site + 2 independent trade-press outlets), unanimous finding: the pipeline's owner and operator is DT Midstream (formerly DTE Midstream Appalachia, LLC), and 'Birdsboro Power' belongs in the picture only as the pipeline's sole shipper/customer and the separate power plant's developer — never as the pipeline's owner. Recommend Owner1='DT Midstream' 100% (replacing 'Birdsboro Power') and Operator='DT Midstream' (currently blank; see fills[]).

validity.recommendation: verify/correct StartLocation — the receipt-point township named by every primary source is Rockland Township, not Oley
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's StartLocation = 'Oley'. Three independent sources describing the pipeline's actual receipt point (the Texas Eastern interconnect where the line begins) all name a DIFFERENT Berks County township: FERC's Order Issuing Certificate para. 4 ('extending from a single receipt point on Texas Eastern's pipeline in Rockland Township, Berks County, Pennsylvania, to a single delivery point at a new... facility... in Birdsboro'); Marcellus Drilling News, June 2018 ('a 14-mile natural gas pipeline from the Texas Eastern Transmission (Tetco) mainline in Rockland Township, to a natural gas-fired power plant... in Birdsboro'); and MDN again, Dec 2018 ('Construction began on a new 14-mile pipeline from the Texas Eastern Transmission (Tetco) mainline in Rockland Township, to a natural gas-fired power plant... in Birdsboro'). None of the sources read name Oley as the origin point. Oley Township DOES appear repeatedly in the FERC order and EA — but only as a township the ROUTE crosses partway through (the order discusses HDD crossings of an Oley Township sewer line and impacts to the Oley Township Historic District), not as the start point. Oley Township and Rockland Township are distinct, adjacent Berks County townships; GEM's StartLocation appears to have recorded a mid-route township the pipeline passes through rather than the actual origin/receipt-point township named by every source. EndLocation='Birdsboro' and both StartState/Province and EndState/Province='Pennsylvania' are all correct and not contested. Recommend StartLocation be corrected to 'Rockland Township' (or 'Rockland Township, Berks County'), pending Baird's confirmation of GEM's exact locality-naming convention for a receipt-point-only location.

validity.recommendation: minor — consider correcting ConstructionMonth from 5 (May) to 6 (June); not material enough to certainly overturn without a primary-source month
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records ConstructionYear=2018, ConstructionMonth=5. The two Marcellus Drilling News articles that discuss construction timing both point to June, not May: the June 12, 2018 piece is headlined 'Construction Begins for 14-Mile Pipe' and describes preliminary clearing as newly underway that week; the December 2018 piece, recapping the project, states 'Construction began on a new 14-mile pipeline... in June' explicitly. Both articles are the same publisher (one origin), so this is not two independent sources agreeing on June — it's a single trade-press outlet reporting the same fact twice, months apart, with no contradiction. No source read states 'May' specifically; the original FERC pre-filing letter and the Nov-2017 NGI brief both describe an earlier PLANNED construction start ('early [2018]' / January 2018 per DTE's original schedule), which did not hold — actual mobilization visibly began around June per MDN. Given the single-publisher caveat, this is flagged as a spec caveat rather than a hard concern; ConstructionYear=2018 is solidly confirmed either way.

summary: P0370 confirmed real, correctly classified, not a duplicate; length/diameter/capacity/status all corroborated by FERC order + independent trade press. Two attribution concerns: Owner1 should be DT Midstream, not Birdsboro Power (which is only the pipeline's customer and the power plant's separate developer); StartLocation should be Rockland Township, not Oley (the receipt point, per FERC + 2 independent MDN articles). Minor spec caveat on ConstructionMonth (single-publisher evidence points to June, not May). FuelSource left UNRESOLVED — no named upstream field, only an interstate-mainline interconnect.
